name: Kinone-bashi (the Kashiwara Great Zelkova)

location.address: Kashiwara-cho, Kashiwara 1, Tamba City, Hyogo Prefecture

access: Free. Stands beside the approach to Kashiwara Hachiman Shrine near the Tamba City Kashiwara branch office, open to the public.
transport: Short walk from JR Kashiwara Station on the JR Fukuchiyama Line.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree with a genuinely unusual feature: one major root grew thick enough to span the roughly 6m-wide Okumura River underground for about 10m, forming what looks like a natural bridge across the riverbank, hence the name Kinone-bashi ('tree-root bridge'). Stands beside the approach to Kashiwara Hachiman Shrine, founded 1024. Designated a Hyogo Prefecture Natural Monument on 30 March 1970. girth_cm (640) is the breast-height girth per the city's own page; height approx 21m, branch spread approx 25m in each direction, the largest zelkova in Tamba City. Currently under treatment for Armillaria tabescens (Naratake Modoki) fungal infection, which entered through roots damaged by past road and bridge construction; the city has been actively treating it (removing decayed wood, applying antagonistic fungi) since 2002. Flagged for the ongoing disease treatment, which the story should mention honestly rather than presenting the tree as untroubled.
